A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DesignX work and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. The additions and renumbering can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and realistic optimization experiments, ablations, scaling analyses, and appendix comparisons with LLM-generated optimizers.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a static-workflow control, runtime measurements, and a rank-based analysis.

M1.justification: The 116-module Modular-EC space, autoregressive workflow generator, dynamic hyperparameter controller, and REINFORCE/PPO training procedure remain unchanged, including Appendix D. Renaming hyperparameter control as dynamic algorithm configuration and correcting Wtoken to Wfeature do not change the method. SBS is an added experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic single/composition/hybrid optimization problems and Protein-Docking, HPO-B, and UAV tasks. The added controls and analyses introduce no new dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds SBS, a retrained feature-free DesignX control, and CMA-ES to the ablation comparison. CMA-ES already participated in the original benchmark comparison, but its inclusion here is new. The main benchmark and appendix LLM comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new SBS experiment zeros instance and observation features during retraining. Section 4.4 also introduces individual-method rank evaluation using the existing Table 1 rollouts and reports timing comparisons. Original data splits, optimization budgets, model settings, and benchmark evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The ablation study now tests whether problem-dependent features and customized workflows help relative to SBS, with CMA-ES as an additional reference. Runtime decomposition and rank-based supplementary analyses are added. Existing agent-removal, scaling, module-choice, and initialization analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds a critical-difference diagram and rank-based significance discussion in Figure 8, using existing rollout data. The original 51-independent-run reporting and uncertainty displays remain unchanged; no increased run count is stated. The new analysis does not specify its statistical test or significance threshold.

E6.justification: New results include SBS and CMA-ES distributions in Figure 6, near-equal ranks for CMA-ES and DesignX in Figure 8, and runtime measurements in Table 2. Section 4.4 reports average problem-solving times of 5.5 seconds for DesignX versus 5.0 seconds for CMA-ES. Existing Table 1 scores and appendix results, including the LLM comparison, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, feature formulas, and synthetic-problem construction remain unchanged. The feature-embedder symbol correction is not a mathematical revision. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Joint workflow generation and dynamic configuration, human-competitive generalization, and learned design insights remain the central contributions. The novelty bullet is reframed, but the abstract, introductory superiority claims, and conclusion retain their substantive scope. The new qualifications appear in the discussion.

C2.justification: New Section 4.4 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: it acknowledges near-parity with CMA-ES under individual ranks, explains computational bottlenecks, and explicitly identifies single-objective scope and six-day training cost as limitations. The SBS discussion newly argues for customized workflows. These additions materially qualify the previously dominant superiority narrative; the existing HPO-B limitation in Appendix F.3 remains.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly discloses per-process training times and totals of 7.5k Agent-1 steps and 2.2M Agent-2 steps; Section 4.4 explains CPU execution. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and pseudocode are retained. The separate pointer to complete per-instance results is removed, although the same repository link remains in the abstract.

R1.justification: Seven references are added: four concerning lifelong optimizer generation, surrogate learning, neural landscape analysis, and instance generation, plus three supporting comparisons with L2O, programming by optimization, and CASH. These extend research positioning without replacing the original related-work account or adding evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.4 and funding acknowledgments, refines the introductory contribution wording, renames the agent subsections, and makes localized terminology and notation edits. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime Table 2 and rank-comparison Figure 8, expands Figure 6 from four to six distributions, and restyles Figure 2. Figure 3 moves onto the Table 1 page, and appendix figures and tables are renumbered. Most existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The SBS control, runtime breakdown, and individual-method rank comparison make the evaluation more informative. Acknowledging CMA-ES near-parity and explicit applicability limits improves calibration beyond v1's grouped-average comparisons. The gains remain limited because broad superiority language persists in the abstract and the new significance analysis lacks a specified test and threshold.
